text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Philips Electronics posts good Q2 profit growth as a result of restructuring activities. (p1)
- Number of working people aged over 50 rose in 1996 for the first time in decades. (p1)
- Dutch government issues a guide to the U.S. capital market. (p3)
- Consumer spending in the Netherlands rose 3.6 percent last May. (p5)
- Weak guilder against the mark feeds speculation about a rate hike. (p11)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- TV producer Endemol extends in Spain by taking a 45 pct stake in rival Zeppelin. (p2)
- Philips created 800 new jobs, but slashed 2,000 other jobs in the Netherlands. (p2)
- Automation firms have a hard time finding qualified staff. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Cabinet studies possibilities to extend tax advantages on green investments abroad. (p19)
- Growing number of businesses take advantage of government fiscal scheme for investments in environment-friendly or energy-saving techniques. (p19)
TROUW
- One out of every three investment funds performs below par, according to a consumer organisation. (p7)
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm defends share option schemes. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Sanitary ware maker Sphinx Gustavsberg targets wealthy Russians. (p10)
